newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Lithuanian pianist wins Reuters Young Artist Prize.
newsitem.headline: Lithuanian pianist wins Reuters Young Artist Prize.

text.p: Lithuanian pianist Kasparas Uinskas was awarded the 1997 Reuters Young Artists Scholarship on Saturday at the Verbier Festival & Academy, a classical music and performing arts festival in Switzerland.

The scholarship, awarded annually by the Reuter Foundation to assist talented young musicians in their studies, is worth 12,000 Swiss francs ($7,860) and includes an invitation to play at next years festival in the Swiss Alpine resort of Verbier.
The winner is selected during master-classes and workshops held during the two-week event, a company statement said.

Uinskas' performance was judged by two piano professors from New York's Juilliard School, American/Israeli Joseph Kalichstein and Bella Davidovich, born in Azerbaijan, the 1949 winner of the Chopin competition in Warsaw.
Uinskas, 18, is currently studying music in the Lithuanian capital Vilnius and completing schooling in his home town of Druskieniki. He is preparing for exams to enter the Academy of Music in Warsaw.
Joint winners last year were Russian-born pianist Alexandra Trussov, 20, and her violinist brother Kirill, 16, who live in Luebeck, Germany.

Reuters, a leading international information organisation which provides news, financial data, dealing systems and information management systems to nearly 400,000 users in financial markets and media worldwide, is a founding co-sponsor of the four-year-old Verbier Festival & Academy.
